name: Otter, Giant
body:
GIANT OTTER
CR 2

Otters have long, slim bodies and relatively short limbs, with webbed paws. Most have sharp claws on their feet and all except the sea otter have long, muscular tails.

XP 600
N Medium animal
Init +7; Senses low-light vision, scent; Perception +5

DEFENSE

AC 17, touch 14, flat-footed 13 (+3 Dex, +1 dodge, +3 natural)
hp 26 (4d8+8)
Fort +6, Ref +7, Will +2

OFFENSE

Speed 20 ft., swim 40 ft.
Melee bite +6 (1d6+3), 2 claws +1 (1d4+1)
Space 5 ft.; Reach 5 ft.
Special Attacks musk (DC 14), rake (1 claw +1, 1d4+1)

STATISTICS

Str 16, Dex 17, Con 15, Int 2, Wis 13, Cha 10
Base Atk +3; CMB +6; CMD 20 (24 vs. trip); +2 when swimming
Feats Dodge, Improved Initiative
Skills Perception +5, Stealth +8 (+12 in water), Swim +15; Racial Modifiers +4 Stealth in water

SPECIAL ABILITIES

Hold Breath (Ex)

An otter can hold its breath for 4 rounds per point of Constitution.

Musk (Ex)

When a creature adjacent to the otter hits it with a melee attack, it can spray that creature with musk as an immediate action. The attacker is sickened for 1d4 rounds (DC 14 Fortitude negates), and the unpleasant stench lingers on the creature for 1 hour. The otter must wait 1d4 rounds before using its musk again. The save DC is Constitution-based.

River Rake (Ex)

When swimming, the otter can use the attack action at any point during its movement (or attack at any point during a charge action), completing its movement for the round after attacking. If it hits with this attack, it can use its rake special attack.

Slippery Swimmer (Ex)

An otter’s movement does not provoke attacks of opportunity when it is swimming, and it gains a +2 circumstance bonus to its CMD when swimming.

ECOLOGY

Environment cold forests, rivers, or coastal
Organization solitary or pair
Treasure none

These playful mammals are well adapted for semi-aquatic life, as their thick fur keeps them warm even in cold water. They are clever creatures with their paws, able to manipulate rocks and shells as crude tools. Their fur tends toward dark brown, lighter on the face and belly, and they can slide quickly on wet grass, mud, and snow. Their dens are typically burrows along riverbanks with underwater entrances for the safety of their young. In addition to common predators, they are sometimes hunted for their sleek fur. They are highly social, with complex yips and barks used for communication.

Giant otters follow many of the habits of their lesser river and sea otter kin, though they can be more aggressive hunters and are more active during daytime whereas smaller otters often hunt during twilight hours, with their whiskers helping locate prey even in dark or cloudy waters. Giant otters can live in groups of up to 10, usually led by a dominant breeding pair. They are very territorial and will attack humans or any other intruders into their ranges. They grow to nearly 10 feet long and weigh over 100 pounds.
